discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori proposed the 'magic wavelength' optical lattice, which removes the light shift that people had assumed was unavoidable when trapping atoms. Many neutral atoms can then be interrogated at once, free of motional effects. He and Ye turned this idea into strontium and ytterbium lattice clocks whose fractional uncertainty is now at the 10^-18 level and beyond, better than caesium by more than two orders of magnitude. Ye added spin-squeezed and many-body-engineered clocks, frequency-comb-based comparisons and resolution of the gravitational redshift over millimetre heights. Katori showed that transportable clocks can do relativistic geodesy in the field. The work builds on the frequency-comb revolution. It has led to plans to redefine the SI second, new searches for dark matter and for variation of fundamental constants, and chronometric geodesy. It is precision measurement that changes both technology and fundamental physics.
